newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: TENNIS-WEARY MUSTER BREEZES PAST FRENCH QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WEARY MUSTER BREEZES PAST FRENCH QUALIFIER.

text.p: Thomas Muster breezed past French qualifier Sebastien Grosjean 6-3 6-3 in the first round of the $425,000 St. Poelten clay-court tennis tournament on Monday, then said he was not 100 percent fit.
Local hero and top seed Muster admitted to still feeling weakend from the dehydration suffered in last week's Italian Open, where he bowed out to unseeded Australian Scott Draper in three sets.
"But I am happy about every victory. It gives me confidence," said Muster, adding he desperately needed more match practice before next week's French Open.
The 1995 French Open champion was widely lauded the king of clay after winning 111 matches on the surface in 1995 and 1996, but this season he has been anything but impressive with three wins.
World number five Muster now faces the winner of Tuesday's first-round clash between Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch and Argentine Hernan Gumy.

In other first-round matches, fourth-seeded Briton Tim Henman crashed out to unfancied Dutchman Sjeng Schalken 6-4 6-2, while sixth-seeded Swede Jonas Bjoerkman lost to Austrian wild card entry Clemens Trimmel 7-5 3-6 7-5.
